title: OpenAI achieves breakthrough creative AI math solution #openai #aicreativity #mathbreakthrough
description:
OpenAI solved one of the most famous unsolved math problems using an AI model that demonstrated genuine creativity rather than brute force. This breakthrough marks a pivotal moment where AI moved beyond rapid computation to innovative problem-solving, creating novel chains of reasoning previously unseen by researchers.

By unlocking AI’s ability to think creatively, this advancement opens new horizons for scientific discovery across fields such as medicine, materials science, and physics. The implications extend to accelerated innovation and potential solutions to complex global challenges through AI-driven insights that were once considered uniquely human.

This milestone, achieved in May 2026, signals a transformative shift in how AI can contribute not only to mathematics but also to broader scientific and technological progress, fundamentally changing the future of human-AI collaboration.

And what did it solve? AI has its limits. If you know how it works, it's really easy to trick it. Also, there's AI is really bad at explaining and this shows that it's not understanding what it's writing. 

For example, let it count vocals without writing helpers into the context window. It won't be able to do it.

Also, most of these math problems aren't solved by pure llms. They use a symbolic AI and they just move a tree down and check all possibilities. 

Why? Because the AI is limited by the same restrictions as a human. It can't see into the future. So it has to do the calculation before it can know it's wrong or true.

I really wished people would be more honest. Nobody is surprised when a calculator solves a calculation is faster. The AI is built to do something and it will be better at that, than a human.
